title: Incident Management

sections.heading: Key concepts
sections.content: An incident represents an unplanned interruption to a service or a degradation of its quality. The standard state lifecycle is: New → In Progress → On Hold → Resolved → Closed (with Canceled as an alternative state). Priority is not entered directly by the user: it is calculated from an Impact x Urgency matrix.

sections.heading: Important fields and relationships
sections.content: Assignment group (the responsible team) is distinct from Assigned to (the specific person). A major incident is flagged via the 'Major Incident' field/process. Incidents can be linked to Problems (root cause) and to Changes (origin of the problem), and an incident can have children (child incidents) attached to a parent incident during a major incident affecting multiple users.

sections.heading: SLA
sections.content: SLAs (Service Level Agreements) define contractual resolution/response times. OLAs (Operational Level Agreements) are the internal equivalent between teams. The 'Reopen count' field increments whenever a Resolved/Closed incident is reopened.

pieges: Confusing priority and urgency: priority is derived (Impact x Urgency) and is generally not directly editable depending on the configuration.
Thinking a Resolved incident is equivalent to Closed: Resolved awaits confirmation/automatic closure after a delay before moving to Closed.
Forgetting that a Problem is used to address the root cause, while an Incident aims for rapid service restoration.
